title: A Current for the Trail
premise: Desert ranger Theo Ashgrove, who has spent seven years outrunning a past he refuses to name, is sent to find a vanished government survey team in the Redstone Range. The trail leads to a hidden river running beneath the desert — the same water source his old expedition destroyed years ago, and the reason one of the surveyors, a woman named Ilsa Vane, has been hunting him since. To survive the crossing before the early snows seal the passes, Theo must guide the surviving surveyors through the underground current while confronting what he buried with it. The book ends with Theo choosing to stay at the range as its keeper rather than return to the life of endless miles, finally trading distance for belonging.
about_author: Edmund Dunmore is the pen name of a former field cartographer who spent a decade mapping arid basins across the American Southwest before turning to fiction. His novels are known for their austere landscapes and characters who measure redemption in terrain rather than words.

chapters.title: Miles Instead of Years
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Tracking a horse thief across the flats, Theo reflects on seven years of deliberate rootlessness, counting miles to avoid memory. He catches the thief but is recalled: a survey team has vanished near Redstone Range, leaving intact gear and no tracks. The emotional beat is restless avoidance — Theo accepts the assignment because any direction is better than standing still.

chapters.title: Gear Without Ghosts
chapters.summary: Theo's POV, shifting to shared POV with surveyor Ilsa Vane when he finds her alive in a slot canyon. The camp was abandoned cleanly; one member, Pell, is missing. Ilsa recognizes Theo and goes cold — she knows about the dried-up spring from his old expedition. The beat is suspicion sharpening into uneasy alliance as snow clouds gather over the high passes.

chapters.title: The Current Beneath
chapters.summary: Climax. Following Pell's traces into a limestone sink, they discover the lost river still flowing underground — the water Theo's crew diverted and covered up. Pell, injured and half-mad, confronts Theo with the truth; Ilsa must choose between justice for her brother, who died when the spring failed, and getting everyone out before the storm closes the pass. The beat is confession under pressure.

chapters.title: What the Snow Keeps
chapters.summary: Resolution. They cross ahead of the snows, carrying Pell out alive; Ilsa files no report, deciding the range itself is punishment enough. Offered reassignment anywhere, Theo requests permanent posting as keeper of the Redstone station — the first place he has ever asked to stay. The beat is quiet arrival: miles become a home, and memory becomes something carried rather than fled.
